name: Posterior subcapsular cataract
summary: A granular plaque just inside the posterior capsule at the visual axis: dark against the red reflex, with glare and poor near vision.
severity_scale: Posterior subcapsular 1-3 (approximately LOCS III P1-P5 by area)

revealed_by.retroillumination: A central dark granular plaque silhouetted against the red reflex.
revealed_by.optic_section_lens: Bright granular opacity at the very back of the lens section, just in front of the posterior capsule.

teaching_points: Focus on the back of the lens in the optic section, and confirm with retroillumination through a dilated pupil.
Ask about steroid use and diabetes, and about glare and near vision, which suffer early.
A small central plaque can reduce vision far more than its size suggests, especially in bright light.

provenance.source: LOCS III: Chylack et al. (1993); values render-calibrated
